lessons.title: Present Perfect
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 2.0: Lesson 1 – Present Perfect (jadval + kombinatsiya + mashqlar).
objectives: Present Perfect qolipini (have/has + V3) tasdiq, inkor va savolda tuza olish.
"ever / never / been to" bilan hayotiy tajriba haqida gapira olish.
20 ta hikoya fe'lining V1–V2–V3 shakllarini yoddan bilish (CORE).
Kombinatsiya: formula → gap → tarjima 1 daqiqada 4 marta.
materials: Narrative verbs (hikoya fe'llari, V1–V2–V3) CORE 20 varag'i.
timeline: "What have you done today?" — ustoz 3 o'quvchidan so'raydi, javoblarni doskaga yozadi (I have eaten…, I have come…).
20 savol, 15 soniya; oldingi dars lug'ati + grammatikasi.
YOZMA NORMATIV — IELTS 1.0 yakuni — Past Simple lug'ati
Kitob jadvali: Positive S+have/has+V3 → Negative haven't/hasn't+V3 → Question Have/Has+S+V3. Har qatorda misol + tarjima, keyin o'quvchi o'zi misol tuzadi.
Har so'z bilan yangi grammatika qolipida gap.
Kitob: formula → gap → tarjima; warm-up / normativ / coin me'yorlari.
Yangi grammatika bilan 5 gap (yozma) yoki 1 daqiqa og'zaki.
Ko'p uchragan xatolar doskada; STRONG lug'at kuchlilarga.

intro: Present Perfect — o'tgan zamonda bo'lgan, lekin natijasi HOZIR ko'rinadigan ish. Vaqt aytilmaydi: "I have lost my key" (kalitim yo'q — hozir).
Past Simple'dan farqi: Past Simple'da vaqt aniq (yesterday, in 2020), Present Perfect'da vaqt muhim emas — natija muhim.
have/has — yordamchi; asosiy fe'l 3-shaklda (V3). Regular: V+ed; irregular — jadvaldan yod olinadi (bugungi lug'at).
formulas: I have started my business recently.
Have you ever been to Tashkent?
have been to = borib kelgan; have gone to = ketgan (hali u yerda)
Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.
Has she called? — Yes, she has.
presentation: Have you ever broken a bone?
Yes, I have. I have broken my arm.
Has your teacher come?
No, she hasn't come yet.
What have you eaten today?
I have eaten plov.
Have they finished the test?
Yes, they have finished it.
Has he ever seen the sea?
No, he has never seen the sea.
Have you done your homework?
Yes, I have done it.
Where has Ali gone?
He has gone to the bank.
Have you been to Samarkand?
Yes, I have been there twice.
Has it rained today?
No, it hasn't rained.
How many books have you read this year?
I have read five books.
notes: Vaqt so'zi bo'lsa (yesterday, last week, ago, in 2019) — Past Simple, Present Perfect emas.
Present Perfect bilan yuradigan so'zlar: ever, never, just, already, yet, recently, so far, today, this week.
"been to" — borib qaytgan; "gone to" — hali qaytmagan. Ustoz doskada ikkita rasm bilan ko'rsatadi.
Irregular V3 — kombinatsiya bilan emas, lug'at bilan yodlanadi: bugungi CORE 20 shu maqsadda.
mistakes: Have you ever been in London?
Have you ever been TO London?
He has been to Paris, he isn't here.

how: CORE 20 — hikoyalarda eng ko'p uchraydigan irregular fe'llar (3 shakli bilan). STRONG +20 va SUPER +20 — kuchli o'quvchi uchun.

lessons.title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
lessons.grammar_topic: PRESENT PERFECT vs PAST SIMPLE (vaqt aniqmi — natijami?)
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 2.0: Lesson 2 – Present Perfect vs Past Simple (jadval, A–E mashqlar).
objectives: Vaqt ko'rsatkichiga qarab Past Simple yoki Present Perfect'ni to'g'ri tanlash.
Bir vaziyatni ikki zamon bilan ifodalash (I have lost it → I lost it yesterday).
Tug'ilish mavzusidagi 20 so'z bilan oila haqida gapira olish.
Kombinatsiya: 1 daqiqada 5 marta.
timeline: "When did you come to Jony Academy?" (Past Simple) → "How many lessons have you had?" (Present Perfect). Ikkisi doskaga: qaysi birida vaqt bor?
20 savol, 15 soniya; oldingi dars lug'ati + grammatikasi.
Kitob jadvali: Past Simple — vaqt aniq (two minutes ago); Present Perfect — vaqt aytilmaydi, natija hozir. Har juft gapni yonma-yon yozib, "when?" so'rab tekshiriladi.
Har so'z bilan yangi grammatika qolipida gap.
Kitob: formula → gap → tarjima; warm-up / normativ / coin me'yorlari.
Yangi grammatika bilan 5 gap (yozma) yoki 1 daqiqa og'zaki.
Ko'p uchragan xatolar doskada; STRONG lug'at kuchlilarga.

intro: Past Simple: ish O'TGANDA bo'ldi va tugadi, VAQTI aniq (yesterday, ago, last…, in 2019, when I was…).
Present Perfect: ish o'tganda bo'ldi, lekin vaqt muhim emas; natija yoki tajriba HOZIR muhim (ever, never, just, already, yet, so far, today).
Suhbat qoidasi: birinchi savol Present Perfect ("Have you ever been to Dubai?"), tafsilot Past Simple ("When did you go? — I went in 2023").
formulas: I entered the room two minutes ago.
Have you ever…? → When did you…?
Have you ever been to Dubai? — Yes. — When did you go? — In 2023.
yesterday / last week / ago / in 2019 → Past Simple
today / this week / this year / so far → Present Perfect
She has called me twice today.
U bugun ikki marta qo'ng'iroq qildi.
I have lost my key. I can't get in.
presentation: Have you ever seen a newborn baby?
Yes, I have. I saw my cousin's baby last month.
When was your brother born?
He was born in 2015.
Has your aunt had her baby yet?
Yes, she has. She gave birth last week.
Did you visit them in hospital?
Yes, I visited them on Monday.
How many times have you been to a baby shower?
I have been to two.
What did you buy for the baby?
I bought a small blanket.
Have your parents chosen a name?
Yes, they have already chosen it.
Did the baby sleep well last night?
No, she cried all night.
Has the baby started walking?
Not yet. She has just started crawling.
When did you last hold a baby?
I held my nephew yesterday.
notes: "ago" faqat Past Simple bilan: two days ago — I met him two days ago.
"just / already / yet" — Present Perfect (Britaniya normasi). Amerikada Past Simple ham bo'ladi, imtihonda Present Perfect yozamiz.
"today / this week" — davr hali tugamagan → Present Perfect; "this morning" tushdan keyin aytilsa → Past Simple.
Savol "When…?" — har doim Past Simple ("When have you…?" bo'lmaydi).
mistakes: I lost my key, I can't get in.
I have lost my key. I can't get in.

lessons.title: Since vs For, Because + Present Perfect
lessons.grammar_topic: HOW LONG? SINCE vs FOR; BECAUSE + PRESENT PERFECT
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 2.0: Lesson 3 – How long: since vs for (jadval, mashqlar F–H, since/for 20 gap).
objectives: since (boshlanish nuqtasi) va for (davomiylik) farqini bilish va ishlatish.
"How long have you…?" savolini tuzish va to'liq javob berish.
"because + Present Perfect" bilan hozirgi holatning sababini aytish.
Nikoh mavzusidagi 20 so'z bilan oila tarixini aytib berish.
timeline: "How long have you studied English?" — javoblar doskaga: "since 2024" / "for two years". Qaysi biri boshlanish nuqtasi, qaysi biri davomiylik?
Kahoot — Present Perfect vs Past Simple
20 savol, 15 soniya; oldingi dars lug'ati + grammatikasi.
YOZMA NORMATIV — Present Perfect vs Past Simple lug'ati
Kitob jadvali: SINCE + boshlangan vaqt, FOR + qancha davom etgani, BECAUSE + Present Perfect (sabab natija hozir), HOW LONG + have/has + S + V3.
Har so'z bilan yangi grammatika qolipida gap.
Kitob: formula → gap → tarjima; warm-up / normativ / coin me'yorlari.
Yangi grammatika bilan 5 gap (yozma) yoki 1 daqiqa og'zaki.
Ko'p uchragan xatolar doskada; STRONG lug'at kuchlilarga.

intro: SINCE — qachon boshlangan: since 2012, since Monday, since I was a child (nuqta).
FOR — qancha davom etgan: for 20 years, for two hours, for a long time (davr).
Ikkalasi ham ko'pincha Present Perfect bilan: ish o'tganda boshlangan, hozir ham davom etyapti.
BECAUSE + Present Perfect: hozirgi holatning sababi o'tgan ishda — "She can't go because she has caught a cold".
formulas: S + have/has + V3 + since + boshlanish nuqtasi
I have lived there for 20 years.
Men u yerda 20 yildan beri yashayman.
How long have you known her?
She can't go to the party because she has caught a cold.
U bazmga bora olmaydi, chunki shamollab qolgan.
I haven't seen him since Monday.
It's two years since we got married.
presentation: How long have you known your best friend?
I have known him since primary school.
How long have your parents been married?
They have been married for twenty years.
Why can't Ali come to the wedding?
Because he has broken his leg.

Since when have you lived in this flat?
Since 2020.

Because she has just got engaged.

For a week.
Why can't you open the door?
Because I have lost my key.
How long has it been since the wedding?
It's been two years since the wedding.
Why isn't he at work?
Because he has gone on holiday.
notes: since + nuqta (yil, kun, soat, voqea); for + raqam + davr (days, weeks, years).
"since I was a child" — since'dan keyin butun gap Past Simple'da keladi.
"How long…?" ga javob: "for / since" bilan; "When…?" ga javob: Past Simple + vaqt.
because + Present Perfect — sabab hozir ta'sir qilyapti; because + Past Simple — sabab o'tgan, tugagan.
mistakes: I have lived here since three years.
I have lived here for three years.
How long do you know him?
How long have you known him?
She is tired because she works all day. (bugun)
She is tired because she has worked all day.

objectives: yet / still / already / just so'zlarining o'rni va ma'nosini bilish.

Kahoot — Since vs For, Because + Present Perfect
20 savol, 15 soniya; oldingi dars lug'ati + grammatikasi.
YOZMA NORMATIV — Since vs For, Because + Present Perfect lug'ati
Kitob jadvali: YET (inkor va savol, gap oxirida) → STILL (inkor, have'dan oldin) → ALREADY (tasdiq, have bilan V3 orasida) → JUST (hozirgina, have bilan V3 orasida). Har biriga 2 misol + tarjima.

intro: YET — "hali": inkor va savolda, GAP OXIRIDA. She hasn't bought anything yet. Has John bought a car yet?

ALREADY — "allaqachon": tasdiqda, have va V3 ORASIDA. I've already spent my salary.
JUST — "hozirgina": have va V3 ORASIDA. He has just gone out.

intro: Present Perfect Continuous — ish o'tganda boshlangan va HOZIRGACHA davom etyapti (yoki hozirgina to'xtadi, izi ko'rinadi).
Urg'u — jarayon va davomiylik: "I have been waiting for two hours" (2 soatdan beri kutyapman).
Present Perfect esa natijaga urg'u beradi: "I have waited" (kutdim — tugadi). Farqi 6-darsda chuqur o'rganiladi.
Holat fe'llari (know, like, have=ega bo'lmoq, be) continuous'da ishlatilmaydi: "I have known him" (has been knowing — xato).
formulas: She hasn't been singing for a long time.
Have you been watching the games?
How long + have/has + S + been + V-ing?
How long have you been learning English?
… been + V-ing + for davr / since nuqta
It has been raining since morning.
I'm tired because I've been running.

notes: for + davr, since + nuqta — 3-dars qoidasi shu yerda ham.
Holat fe'llari (know, believe, own, love) — Present Perfect Simple: "I have known her for years".
"all day / all morning / lately / recently" — Present Perfect Continuous bilan tez-tez keladi.
Tana a'zolari bilan: "My head has been aching" = "I have had a headache".
mistakes: I have been knowing him for years.

reading.title: Topic 1. A Restaurant for Change
text: Jamie Oliver wants to change people's lives and he is using food to do it. Oliver, a chef, is well-known for sharing his secrets of cooking healthy food through his magazine, cookbooks, and television shows. He is also changing lives through his Italian restaurant, Fifteen.

Fifteen started in London, England, as a place to train young adults to work in a kitchen. Oliver's idea was to create a professional kitchen that can help young people get a fresh start and a chance to become professional chefs. Every September, a new group of 18- to 24-year-olds start work at Fifteen. When they start, they are usually not qualified for a restaurant job, but that will change quickly.

In the 12 months of training, the student chefs study cooking at college and get hands-on training at the restaurant. Besides learning kitchen skills, they learn the importance of using fresh ingredients and how to create their own recipes. The students also learn how to manage money and deal with difficult customers. Overall, the program encourages them to believe in themselves.

The restaurant's name, Fifteen, comes from the number of students the restaurant had when it started in 2002. Today, Oliver has three of these restaurants, and a few hundred students have finished the program. Around 90 percent of the graduates are still working in the food industry. Some own restaurants or work in some of the best kitchens around the world. Others are now starring in their own TV shows.

text: Dear Sir / Madam, I would like to apply for the job of tour leader for your Overland Africa tours. I have had lots of useful experience for this role.

I have spent five months backpacking around Africa. In 2018, I visited Ethiopia, Kenya and Tanzania. I used local transport and organised my own accommodation, food and visas. I have also worked as a leader at a children's summer camp in the south of England. I worked there in 2017. I led activities for children aged 9–12, including football, climbing and campfire songs. For this work, I received training in climbing instruction and first aid. I learned how to be helpful and positive, and how to help people make friends.

Finally, I have completed the Active Youth Challenge. I did this while I was at high school in 2016. I volunteered at a social club for the elderly, learned car mechanics by myself, and organised a four-day camping and hiking trip in the Scottish mountains. This experience taught me about camping equipment and how to deal with problems like bad weather and getting lost.
I believe I have lots of useful experience to work as an Overland Tour Guide. I would love the opportunity to tell you more about my skills at an interview. Yours faithfully, Nicholas Rigby

reading.title: Topic 25. Why aren't babies born on certain days?
text: Do you know anyone whose birthday is Christmas Day? You may know a few, but actually, having a birthday on that day is quite rare.

December 25th is the least common birthday in the USA, Australia and New Zealand. Between 30% and 40% fewer babies are born on this day than on the peak days. In England, Wales and Ireland, Christmas Day is the second rarest day for a birthday. There, the fewest birthdays are on December 26th, the national holiday called Boxing Day. In the USA, the four least common birthdays are Christmas, New Year, Thanksgiving and Independence Day.

So why does this happen? A third of babies in the USA are born by caesarean. Doctors can plan the date for these operations. They don't schedule them for the national holidays because they want to be celebrating, not working.

Some times of year are more common for birthdays than others. In the USA and New Zealand, the most popular month is September. In the UK, it's September or early October. Many babies are conceived in the cold winter months when days are short. In countries further north than the UK, like Norway and Russia, the peak months are earlier: in July or August.
Think about your birthday. Is it at a common time of year? Would you prefer your birthday to be at a different time of year?

intro: Superlative — uch va undan ko'p narsa ichida ENG: the tallest boy in the class.
1 bo'g'in: the + adj-est (the biggest — undosh ikkilanadi; the nicest). -y: the happiest.
2+ bo'g'in: the most + adj (the most beautiful). Istisno: the best, the worst, the furthest, the least, the most.
Superlative'dan keyin: in + joy/guruh (in the world, in our class), of + all (of all my friends). Ko'pincha Present Perfect bilan: "the best film I have ever seen".

Xarakter so'zlarida juftlarni birga yodlang: reliable = trustworthy; hard-working = industrious; sociable = out-going.

reading.title: Topic 23. The man with the most world records
text: Ashrita Furman is a record-breaking record-breaker: he has set more records than anyone else in the world! In the last 40 years, he has established more than 600 records!

As a child, Ashrita loved reading the Guinness Book of World Records. He wanted to be in it too. But he thought people had to be good at sports to be in the book. He wasn't a good athlete. He felt his dream would never come true.

Later in life, Ashrita learned meditation, and with this, he learned that nothing is impossible. He tested this idea in 1978 by entering a 24-hour bike race in New York. Without any training, Ashrita came third! After that, he started thinking about breaking records again. He did 27,000 jumping jacks in 6 hours 45 minutes and became a record holder in 1980.

Today, Ashrita has a long list of records, including: walking the furthest distance with a bike on his chin, cycling the longest distance with a bottle on his head and lighting the most candles on a birthday cake. He says his favourite record was "the longest distance on a pogo stick" — 11.5 miles near Mount Fuji. The most difficult record was "the most forward rolls": in 10 hours 30 minutes, he did 8,341 of them.

If you want to break a world record too, Ashrita gives this advice: "Choose something you enjoy because you will need to practise. And don't give up. Your mind will tell you that something is impossible, but it isn't."
